Fiber vs cable internet: which should you pick?

By Jordan Lee, updated May 2, 2026

Key takeaways

Fiber internet usually gives the same upload and download speed, while cable internet gives much faster download than upload speed for most home plans.

How fiber and cable differ

Fiber sends data as light through glass strands, so the signal loses very little strength over long distances. Cable uses copper coaxial lines that were first built for television.

Because cable is shared by a neighbourhood, speeds can drop in the evening when many people are online at the same time. Fiber networks are less affected by this.

The FCC national broadband map shows which providers serve an address, and users on Reddit often share real speed test results for both kinds of service.

Frequently asked questions

Is fiber faster than cable?

Usually yes, especially for uploads, video calls and online gaming where upload speed and latency matter a great deal.
